_comment: PROVIDER PLUG-IN for the `external-record` role — the SECOND offer, so the role is a choice and not a vendor (HG-0008, decision K9). A Sigstore-style transparency log (Rekor, or an institution's own append-only log with RFC 3161 timestamps): every Loom envelope becomes a signed entry whose inclusion proof and log index are the record id. What it gives that Kosli does not: a public, verifiable inclusion proof with no vendor account. What it does not give: trails, policy evaluation over the record, environment snapshots — rows 2.9–2.11 stay unmounted under this provider, and the status report says so. NO ADAPTER MODULE SHIPS YET for this provider (core/providers/transparency-log.mjs is not in the bundle): selecting it is recorded honestly as 'ships no adapter module' by core/external-record.mjs until one is contributed. To adopt: record the choice in docs/governance/provider-selection.json, copy this file to docs/governance/adapters/, and contribute or commission the adapter.
capability: An append-only, timestamped log entry per Loom envelope with an inclusion proof — asserted by the log, resolvable by log index, never rewritable from the tree the agent edits

config._comment: ADOPT: the log's URL and the public key its signed tree heads verify against.
config.log_public_key: ADOPT: PEM of the log's signing key

reconciliation._comment: The seal gate holds the log index; the provider proves the log holds an entry at that index whose body is the envelope carrying this anchor, and that the inclusion proof verifies against a signed tree head.

activation_evidence._comment: ADOPT: fill from the first entry written and read back with a verified inclusion proof, plus the tamper probe.
activation_evidence.runner_identity: ADOPT: the least-privilege identity that writes entries — must NOT be the coding agent's identity
activation_evidence.tamper_probe: ADOPT: 'rejected' once you have tested that a manifest naming a log index the log does not hold fails scripts/evidence-seal-check.mjs
